cover.headline: The investments are working — but a ₹1.9 Cr protection gap sits underneath a 66%-equity balance sheet. The single most valuable move here is not a better fund; it is closing the term-cover and emergency-fund gaps before another rupee goes into equity. That is the call no single spoke can make.

coverage.lede: Every spoke sees one domain; this is the only view that sees all of them and how they interact. It builds the net-worth spine across the classes no spoke touches — property, gold, EPF, FDs — then weighs investments, protection and cashflow together to answer one question: where does the next rupee go?

spine.title: ₹1.85 Cr — healthy total, thin at the base
spine.lede: The total is real and diversified, but two-thirds sits in equity and only ₹3.7 L is liquid. A strong net worth with a thin liquid base and no protection is a fragile balance sheet, not a safe one.
spine.footer: IndMoney net-worth snapshot + allocation breakdown · positions normalized through holdings.py

legs.title: Each leg's one-line verdict
legs.lede: Three spokes ran in cheap mode and returned a digest each. Two are in good shape; protection is the one that fails its audit — and protection is the domain that overrules the others.
legs.footer: Digests only — full leg reports at artifacts/wealth/2026-08-28.md/legs/

items.name: Investments
items.read: 14.2% avg XIRR across 18 holdings, diversified across caps; the fund sleeve carries no red flags. One single-stock position is >8% of equity — a concentration to trim, not a crisis.

items.name: Protection
items.read: Term life ₹50 L against a ~₹2.4 Cr need (10× income + liabilities, net of assets) — a ₹1.9 Cr shortfall. Health cover is a single ₹5 L family floater, thin for a family of four.

items.name: Cashflow
items.read: ~28% savings rate on ₹1.2 L monthly expenses, no lifestyle-creep flags. The one weakness is downstream: too little of the surplus is being held liquid.

scorecard.title: Strong where it shows, weak where it matters
scorecard.lede: Five domains, each a falsifiable one-liner. The overall grade is the worst assessed domain — because a critical protection gap is not averaged away by strong investments.
scorecard.footer: Status ∈ strong · adequate · weak · critical · not assessed · overall = worst assessed domain

cross.title: The calls no single spoke can make
cross.lede: This is where the whole-picture view earns its place. Each of these reads needs two domains at once — and each overrules the instinct a single spoke would have.
cross.footer: risk_posture is the personal balance-sheet posture — never loosened by a risk-on market

ef.label: EMERGENCY-FUND RUNWAY
ef.note: ₹3.7 L liquid ÷ ₹1.2 L monthly expenses = 3.1 months — inside the target band but at its floor. One job loss or medical event with a thin cover would force selling equity at the worst time.

reads.label: PROTECTION VS NET WORTH
reads.text: On the earner's death the family faces a ₹1.9 Cr shortfall against its needs — the single biggest risk on this balance sheet, and it dwarfs any fund-selection or entry-timing decision.

reads.label: RISK POSTURE
reads.text: Fix-foundation-first. Do not add equity risk — no fresh lump sums, no new single-stock bets — until term cover and the emergency fund are closed. A risk-on market does not change this.

plan.title: Where the next five rupees go
plan.lede: Ordered across domains, not within one. Protection and the emergency fund come before any investment optimization — because the downside they cover is larger than any upside the investments add.
plan.footer: Each action names the spoke to run for depth · max five, most-important first

rows.text: Raise term life cover to ~₹2.4 Cr
rows.step: Get a level-term quote today; buy before any new equity goes in.
Take the family floater to ₹15–25 L via a super top-up.

rows.text: Build the emergency fund to 6 months
rows.step: Add ₹3.6 L to liquid (sweep FD / liquid fund) before fresh SIPs.
Once the foundation is set, cut the >8% position back toward 5%.

rows.text: Check fund overlap in the MF sleeve
rows.step: Review the 24% fund sleeve for duplicate exposure.

gaps.title: What this review does not cover
gaps.lede: The spine is complete; the legs ran cheap and defer their depth. Every uncovered edge is labelled, and the net-worth figures are your own to verify.

items.label: LEG DEPTH DEFERRED
items.text: Each leg ran in cheap mode — the deep portfolio, insurance and budget analyses live in the named spokes. Run them for the full working.

items.label: PROTECTION NEED IS A MODEL
items.text: The ₹2.4 Cr term need is a 10×-income-plus-liabilities estimate; a precise figure needs the household's actual liabilities and goal timeline (insurance-advisor computes it).

items.label: PROPERTY VALUATION
items.text: Real estate is carried at the IndMoney-supplied value — an estimate, not a transacted price; a 20% swing there moves the allocation percentages.

items.label: ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE
items.text: This deck is a design specimen with sample figures. A real run carries your own IndMoney net worth and live leg digests.

gaps.weakest: The weakest link is protection: everything else can wait, but an uninsured earner with dependents is the one exposure that turns a strong balance sheet into a fragile one overnight.
gaps.disclaimer: Net-worth figures are first-party data; verify any action against the source. This is the only cross-domain view — position-level depth belongs to the spokes. Not investment advice — personal research tool.
